purpose: Train one numerical critic to decide whether to take the existing weekly reversal pair or remain in cash. Keep the long and short definitions, clock, lot sizes and funding costs fixed.
features: At the original cutoff use the median seven-day return of the six spot markets and the difference between the highest and lowest such return. From up to 52 previous weeks whose outcomes closed before the cutoff select 12 nearest weeks after scaling each feature by its historical standard deviation. Use the realized net weekly return of the registered reversal comparator on those weeks. At least 26 prior weeks required. Take the pair only when its mean net return minus one sample standard error exceeds zero. No parameter search. Save the neighbors and estimate for each decision.
evaluation: Use the earlier year as the initial experience. Evaluate the last two consecutive 26-week blocks separately, resetting account capital to 1000 each time. Full-book cash weeks are included. Compare to the always-reversal and cash controls. Also calculate a hindsight diagnostic: each week recompute both admissible directions from that diagnostic account's own starting capital and pick the higher net result or cash. This deliberately uses future outcomes and must never supply a model input or a tradable signal.
qualification: Both evaluation blocks must beat cash and always-reversal after costs, stay positive excluding their best week, and reach 2% geometric weekly growth. All these historical periods have been inspected for other strategies. No exchange authority.
